questions.question: Find the surface area of a sphere whose diameter is equal to 98 cm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius (r) = 98 ÷ 2 = 49 cm.

Surface Area = 4 × π × r²

⇒ 4 × (22/7) × 49 × 49

⇒ 88 × 343 = 30,184 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 30,184 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Surface Area of a sphere = 4πr²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = d ÷ 2 = 98 ÷ 2 = 49 cm

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × (22/7) × 49²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × 22 × 7 × 49

⇒ Surface Area = 88 × 343

Volume of a Sphere

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cone is 6500π cm², and the diameter of its base is 100 cm. Find the height (in cm) of the cone.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Base **radius (r)** = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 cm.

**Slant height (l)** = CSA ÷ (πr) = 6500π ÷ (50π) = 130 cm.

Using **Pythagorean triplet** (5, 12, 13) scaled by 10 → (50, 120, 130).

Height (h) = 120 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 6500π cm²

**Diameter (d)** = 100 cm ⇒ **Radius (r)** = 50 cm

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of cone = πrl

Relationship between height (h), radius (r), and slant height (l): l² = r² + h²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/658f4264d65598628b532921a815ce2c35410f01c860a8d583cc52da185efb20.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ π × 50 × l = 6500π

⇒ 50 × l = 6500

⇒ l = 6500 ÷ 50

⇒ l = 130 cm

⇒ h² = l² − r²

⇒ h² = 130² − 50²

⇒ h² = 16900 − 2500

⇒ h² = 14400

⇒ h = √14400 = 120 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cone

It is the sum of the curved surface area and the base area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The amount of space occupied by a cone: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Pythagorean Triplets

Standard sets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) help solve right-triangle geometry problems quickly by scaling.</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cone is 5400π cm², and the diameter of its base is 144 cm. Find the height (in cm) of the cone.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius (r) = 144 ÷ 2 = 72 cm

CSA = πrl ⇒ 5400π = π × 72 × l

l = 5400 ÷ 72 = 75 cm

Using Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25) × 3 → (21, 72, 75)

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 5400π cm²

**Diameter** = 144 cm ⇒ **Radius (r)** = 72 cm

**Formula Used:**

CSA of Cone = πrl

Slant height (l) = √(h² + r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3cf7e7f1262c085f0ba9083b80c202e580ba35a8e08b797a76a0c5a986e52c3b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ π × 72 × l = 5400π

⇒ l = 5400 ÷ 72

⇒ l = 75 cm

⇒ h² = l² − r²

⇒ h² = 75² − 72²

⇒ h² = (75 − 72)(75 + 72)

⇒ h² = 3 × 147

⇒ h² = 441

⇒ h = √441 = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cone

TSA = πr(l + r), which includes the curved area and the circular base area.

Volume of Cone

Volume = (1/3)πr²h, which is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height.

Slant Height Relation

In a right circular cone, l² = h² + r² based on the **Pythagoras Theorem**.</p

questions.question: In a circle, the length of a chord is 12 cm and the perpendicular distance from the centre of the circle to the chord is 5 cm. What is the radius of the circle? (Rounded up to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **perpendicular** from the **centre** bisects the **chord**.

Half-chord = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

Use the **Pythagorean triplet** (5, 12, 13) or calculate √(5² + 6²).

Radius = √(25 + 36) = √61 ≈ 7.81 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.81 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **chord (AB)** = 12 cm

**Perpendicular distance (OM)** = 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a **right-angled triangle**, r² = (chord/2)² + (perpendicular distance)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16379bf8cff2c1448aeaece5b14cbce51f74cc9c4164a628e8f21d99dbe1c3eb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **chord** be AB and the **centre** be O.

⇒ OM is the **perpendicular** from O to AB, so AM = MB = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

⇒ In **ΔOMB**, using **Pythagoras Theorem**:

⇒ OB² = OM² + MB²

⇒ r² = 5² + 6²

⇒ r² = 25 + 36

⇒ r² = 61

⇒ r = √61 ≈ 7.8102...

**∴ The correct answer is 7.81 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Theorem

The **perpendicular** dropped from the **centre** of a circle to a **chord** always bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Radius and Chord Relationship

The distance (d) of the chord from the centre, the radius (r), and the chord length (L) are related by r² = d² + (L/2)².

Equal Chords Property

**Equal chords** of a circle are **equidistant** from the centre of the circle.</p

questions.question: A conical vessel has base radius 31 cm and height 45 cm. Water is poured into the vessel until it is 2/3 full. Find the volume( in cm³) of water in the vessel.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The total volume of the **conical vessel** is V = (1/3) × π × r² × h.

Volume of water = (2/3) × Total Volume = (2/3) × (1/3) × π × r² × h.

Given: **radius (r)** = 31 cm, **height (h)** = 45 cm.

Volume of water = (2/9) × π × 31² × 45 = 2 × π × 961 × 5 = 9610π cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 9610π cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/260d8dbaee0d1d3edf5699f54c66403e68df7e82eb0b2546caf8165e948a87ec.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ **Base radius** of the conical vessel (r) = 31 cm

⇒ **Height** of the conical vessel (h) = 45 cm

⇒ The vessel is filled up to **2/3 of its capacity (volume)**.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Volume of a cone (V) = (1/3) × π × r² × h

⇒ Volume of water = (2/3) × V

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of water = (2/3) × [ (1/3) × π × 31² × 45 ]

⇒ Volume of water = (2/9) × π × 961 × 45

⇒ Volume of water = 2 × π × 961 × 5

⇒ Volume of water = 10 × 961 × π

⇒ Volume of water = 9610π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 9610π cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Right Circular Cone

The volume is exactly one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Slant Height of a Cone

The relation between slant height (l), radius (r), and vertical height (h) is given by Pythagoras theorem: l = √(r² + h²).

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The curved surface area or lateral surface area of a cone is given by: CSA = π × r × l.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the circular base: TSA = πr(l + r).

questions.question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 10 cm is melted and recast into 125 identical spheres. What is the ratio of the surface area of the original sphere to the total surface area of 6 smaller spheres so formed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of spheres **n = 125** ⇒ Radius ratio **R : r = ³√125 : ³√1 = 5 : 1**.

Surface area ratio of 1 large to 1 small = **R² : r² = 5² : 1² = 25 : 1**.

Ratio of 1 large to **6 small** surface areas = **25 : (1 × 6) = 25 : 6**.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Radius of large sphere **R = 10 cm**, Number of small spheres **n = 125**.

**Formula Used:** Volume of sphere = **(4/3)πr³**; Surface area = **4πr²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa2b8496fd98004e8ca2bdd59963ab96f69779aa3040740e303341c55fe47047.png] 

⇒ Volume of large sphere = **125 × Volume of 1 small sphere**

⇒ (4/3)π(10)³ = **125 × (4/3)πr³**

⇒ 1000 = **125 × r³**

⇒ r³ = **1000 ÷ 125 = 8** ⇒ **r = 2 cm**

⇒ Surface area of original sphere (S₁) = **4πR² = 4π(10)² = 400π**

⇒ Total Surface area of 6 small spheres (S₂) = **6 × 4πr² = 24π(2)² = 96π**

⇒ Ratio = **S₁ : S₂ = 400π : 96π**

⇒ Ratio = **400 : 96 = 25 : 6**

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation in Recasting

When a solid object is melted and recast into other shapes, the **total volume remains constant**. Formula: Vₜₒₜₐₗ = n × Vₑₐ꜀ₕ.

Cube Root Relation for Spheres

If one sphere is melted into **n** identical small spheres, the radius ratio is **R/r = ³√n**.

Surface Area Comparison

The total surface area increases when a large object is divided into smaller pieces. Ratio of Area (1 large : n small) = **1 : n¹/³**.</p

questions.question: The sides (in cm) of a right triangle are (x − 13), (x − 26) and x. Its area (in cm²) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **right triangle triplet** by observing the gap between sides.

The sides are **x − 26**, **x − 13**, and **x** (where **x** is the **hypotenuse**).

The common difference is **13**. Scaling the standard **5, 12, 13 triplet** by **13**:

**5×13, 12×13, 13×13 → 65, 156, 169**. Here **169 − 13 = 156** and **169 − 26 = 143** (does not match 65).

Using **x = 78**: Sides are **78 − 26 = 52**, **78 − 13 = 65**, and **78** (Not a triplet). Using **x = 39**: **13, 26, 39** (No).

Correct triplet calculation: **x² = (x−13)² + (x−26)² → x = 65**. Sides: **39, 52, 65** (Scaled **3, 4, 5 triplet** by 13).

**Area = 1/2 × 39 × 52 = 39 × 26 = 1014 cm²**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1014 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sides are (x − 26), (x − 13) and **hypotenuse** x.

**Formula:** **Base² + Perpendicular² = Hypotenuse²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51b9176fe17614d3c86362e77532faa641128e905e47f899a5eb99a37001f469.png] 

⇒ (x − 26)² + (x − 13)² = x²

⇒ (x² − 52x + 676) + (x² − 26x + 169) = x²

⇒ 2x² − 78x + 845 = x²

⇒ x² − 78x + 845 = 0

⇒ x² − 65x − 13x + 845 = 0

⇒ x(x − 65) − 13(x − 65) = 0

⇒ (x − 65)(x − 13) = 0

⇒ x = 65 (Since x − 26 must be positive, x > 26)

⇒ Base = 65 − 26 = 39 cm, Height = 65 − 13 = 52 cm

⇒ Area = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 39 × 52

⇒ Area = 39 × 26 = 1014 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1014 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) can be scaled by a constant k to find other right triangles (3k, 4k, 5k).

Area of Right Triangle

The area is always half the product of the two shorter sides (legs): Area = 1/2 × a × b.

Quadratic Roots Shortcut

For x² − (sum of roots)x + (product of roots) = 0, identify factors of the constant that add up to the middle coefficient.</p

questions.question:
The sides of a rectangular field are 169 m and 154 m long. Its area is equal to the area of a circular field. What is the circumference (in m) of the circular field?

Take pi = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of **circle** = Area of **rectangle**

πr² = 169 × 154

r² = (169 × 154 × 7) ÷ 22 ⇒ r² = 169 × 7 × 7 ⇒ r = 13 × 7 = 91 m

Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 91 = 44 × 13 = 572 m

**∴ The correct answer is 572 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Length (l) = 169 m, Breadth (b) = 154 m

**Formula Used:** Area of rectangle = l × b; Area of circle = πr²; Circumference = 2πr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c58360d26fc9a6a3568296cf48853feb3c287bab050680d906ce3561b1606b81.png] 

⇒ Area of **Rectangular field** = 169 × 154 = 26026 m²

⇒ Area of **Circular field** = πr² = 26026

⇒ (22 ÷ 7) × r² = 26026

⇒ r² = (26026 × 7) ÷ 22

⇒ r² = 1183 × 7 = 8281

⇒ r = √8281 = 91 m

⇒ **Circumference** = 2 × (22 ÷ 7) × 91

⇒ Circumference = 2 × 22 × 13 = 572 m

**∴ The correct answer is 572 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area and Perimeter of Circle

Area = πr² and Circumference (Perimeter) = 2πr, where r is the radius.

Area of Rectangle

Area = Length × Breadth. Perimeter = 2(Length + Breadth).

Relation between Radius and Circumference

If radius is a multiple of 7 (r=7n), the circumference is 44n and area is 154n².</p

questions.question:
Find the volume (in cm³) of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out from a cube with an edge of 8 cm.

Use pi = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For the **largest cone** in a **cube** of side **a**:

**Diameter** of cone = **Height** of cone = side of cube = **8 cm**.

Radius **r** = 8/2 = **4 cm** and height **h** = **8 cm**.

Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 4² × 8 = (1/3) × (22/7) × 128 = 2816 / 21.

**∴ The correct answer is 134 (2/21) cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Edge of the **cube** (a) = **8 cm**.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of **Right Circular Cone** = (1/3) π r² h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/307bd87e099211d0ed296a03360478a4e1bad13173089b8386c751301fe76470.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ When a **cone** is cut from a **cube**, its **base diameter** equals the cube's edge and its **height** equals the cube's edge.

⇒ Radius (r) = 8 ÷ 2 = **4 cm**

⇒ Height (h) = **8 cm**

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × (4)² × 8

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 16 × 8

⇒ Volume = 2816 ÷ 21

⇒ Volume = 134 (2/21) cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 134 (2/21) cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of largest Sphere in a Cube

The diameter of the **largest sphere** that can fit inside a cube is equal to the side of the cube (a). Volume = (4/3) π (a/2)³.

Volume of largest Cylinder in a Cube

For the **largest cylinder**, the diameter and height are both equal to the side of the cube (a). Volume = π (a/2)² a.

Slant Height of Cone

The **slant height** (l) is given by the Pythagorean relation l = √(r² + h²).</p

questions.question: The area of a rectangle increases by 8 m² if its length is increased by 5 m and breadth is decreased by 7 m. If the length is decreased by 5 m and breadth is increased by 8 m, then its area increases by 33 m². What is the perimeter of the original rectangle (in m)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **original length** be L and **breadth** be B.

From condition 1: (L + 5)(B − 7) = LB + 8 ⇒ −7L + 5B = 43

From condition 2: (L − 5)(B + 8) = LB + 33 ⇒ 8L − 5B = 73

Adding both equations: L = 43 + 73 = 116 m

Substitute L in Eq 2: 8(116) − 5B = 73 ⇒ 5B = 928 − 73 = 855 ⇒ B = 171 m

**Perimeter** = 2(L + B) = 2(116 + 171) = 2(287) = 574 m

**∴ The correct answer is 574 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Area = **Length (L) × Breadth (B)**

**Formula Used:**

Area of Rectangle = **L × B**

Perimeter of Rectangle = **2(L + B)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13a0b03c0686a469abf6037a9cd7df4bce39f713b3d649cb6dbd2780f5b4ca23.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Case 1: (L + 5)(B − 7) = LB + 8

⇒ LB − 7L + 5B − 35 = LB + 8

⇒ −7L + 5B = 43 → (Eq. 1)

⇒ Case 2: (L − 5)(B + 8) = LB + 33

⇒ LB + 8L − 5B − 40 = LB + 33

⇒ 8L − 5B = 73 → (Eq. 2)

⇒ Adding Eq. 1 and Eq. 2:

⇒ (−7L + 8L) + (5B − 5B) = 43 + 73

⇒ L = 116 m

⇒ Putting L = 116 in Eq. 2:

⇒ 8(116) − 5B = 73

⇒ 928 − 5B = 73

⇒ 5B = 855 ⇒ B = 171 m

⇒ Perimeter = 2(116 + 171) = 2(287)

⇒ Perimeter = 574 m

**∴ The correct answer is 574 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rectangle

A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles. Opposite sides are equal and parallel. Diagonal length d = √(L² + B²).

Area and Perimeter Relations

For a fixed perimeter, a square (L=B) has the maximum area. For a fixed area, a square has the minimum perimeter.

Percentage Change in Area

If length increases by x% and breadth increases by y%, net change in area = [x + y + (xy/100)]%.</p

questions.question:
The volume of a solid cylinder is 5852 cm³ and its height is 38 cm. What is the total surface area of the solid cylinder? (Round your answer to the nearest integer) 

(Use pi = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume (V) = πr²h ⇒ 5852 = (22/7) × r² × 38

r² = (5852 × 7) ÷ (22 × 38) = 49 ⇒ r = 7 cm

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(h + r) = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × (38 + 7)

TSA = 44 × 45 = 1980 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1980 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Volume** of cylinder (V) = 5852 cm³

**Height** of cylinder (h) = 38 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume (V) = πr²h

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/faa1528e8fc93a37562b6fa50650a35b2d8650d74acb743e2b563ddc0bd4d09a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 5852 = (22/7) × r² × 38

⇒ r² = (5852 × 7) ÷ (22 × 38)

⇒ r² = 40964 ÷ 836 = 49

⇒ r = √49 = 7 cm

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × (38 + 7)

⇒ TSA = 44 × 45

⇒ TSA = 1980 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1980 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder

The area of the curved part only is given by CSA = 2πrh.

questions.question: A river 20 m deep and 36 m wide is flowing at the rate of 2.7 km/hr. The amount of water (in m³) that runs into the sea per minute is _____.

**∴ The correct answer is 32,400 m³.**

⇒ **Volume of water** per minute = Area × Length of water column in 1 min.

⇒ Volume = 720 × 45 = 32,400 m³.

Flow Rate Measurement

Unit Conversion

Volume of a Cuboid

Since the river is treated as a rectangular channel, the volume is V = l × b × h, where 'l' is the distance water travels in the given time.</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is half of its total surface area. If the height is 128 cm, then find the radius (in cm).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** is half of **Total Surface Area (TSA)**, then **CSA** = **Sum of Area of two bases**.

2πrh = 2πr²

This directly implies **Radius (r)** = **Height (h)**.

Given **h** = 128 cm, therefore **r** = 128 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 128 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height (h)** of the cylinder = 128 cm

**Condition:** **Curved Surface Area** = 1/2 × **Total Surface Area**

**Formulas Used:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 2πrh

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 2πr(h + r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6acf626533d892c481440aee207a8acc1e201074dbc657acd794880a406d97d2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πrh = 1/2 × [2πr(h + r)]

⇒ 2πrh = πr(h + r)

⇒ 2h = h + r

⇒ 2h − h = r

⇒ r = h

⇒ r = 128 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 128 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

The amount of space occupied by a cylinder is given by V = πr²h.

Base Area

The area of one circular base of a cylinder is πr².

Relation when CSA = 1/3 TSA

If CSA is one-third of TSA, then 2πrh = 1/3[2πr(h+r)], which simplifies to r = 2h.</p

questions.question: The length, width and height of a cuboid are in the ratio 10 : 17 : 14, and its total surface area is 1096 cm². Find the length (in cm) of the cuboid.

⇒ Let l = 10x, b = 17x, and h = 14x

⇒ 2[170x² + 238x² + 140x²] = 1096

⇒ 2[548x²] = 1096

⇒ 1096x² = 1096

⇒ x² = 1 ⇒ x = 1

⇒ **Length** = 10 × 1 = 10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cuboid

The space occupied by a cuboid is calculated as Length × Width × Height (l × b × h).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is √(l² + b² + h²).

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

questions.question: If the volume of a right circular cone of height 30 cm is 160π cm³, find the diameter of its base.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 160π = (1/3) × π × r² × 30

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

questions.question: The shorter side of a rectangle is 16 cm less than the longer side. The numerical value of its area is equal to 3 times the numerical value of its perimeter. What is the length (in cm) of its longer side?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **longer side** be L and **shorter side** be (L − 16).

Area = 3 × Perimeter ⇒ L(L − 16) = 3 × 2[L + (L − 16)]

L² − 16L = 6(2L − 16) ⇒ L² − 16L = 12L − 96

L² − 28L + 96 = 0 ⇒ (L − 24)(L − 4) = 0

Since L > 16 (as shorter side L − 16 must be positive), L = 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b43df18acc6d864c27ce2aad6cc85ca722371291cf0f2f01200497253774f6f3.png] 

**Given:**

**Longer side** = L

**Shorter side** = L − 16

**Area** = L(L − 16)

**Perimeter** = 2(L + L − 16) = 2(2L − 16) = 4L − 32

**Calculations:**

⇒ L(L − 16) = 3 × (4L − 32)

⇒ L² − 16L = 12L − 96

⇒ L² − 28L + 96 = 0

⇒ L² − 24L − 4L + 96 = 0

⇒ L(L − 24) − 4(L − 24) = 0

⇒ (L − 24)(L − 4) = 0

⇒ L = 24 or L = 4

If L = 4, then Shorter side = 4 − 16 = −12 (Not possible).

⇒ L = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rectangle Mensuration

The **Area** of a rectangle is length × breadth, and the **Perimeter** is 2 × (length + breadth).

Diagonal of Rectangle

The **Diagonal** (d) is calculated using the Pythagorean theorem: d = √(L² + B²).

Quadratic Roots Property

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.</p

questions.question: The length of a rectangular park is 27 m more than its breadth. Its area is 2268 m². Its breadth (in m) is:

Identify two numbers with a **difference of 27** whose **product is 2268**.

Check options for **breadth (b)**: If b = 36, then length (l) = 36 + 27 = 63.

Product: 36 × 63 = 2268. This matches the given **area**.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:** Area of Rectangle = length × breadth

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25155dfe7b45b6ad6b5dd08e6eca156c9b8f0b900529fbd468948f0afea682f7.png] 

⇒ Area = b × (b + 27) = 2268

⇒ b² + 27b − 2268 = 0

⇒ b² + 63b − 36b − 2268 = 0

⇒ b(b + 63) − 36(b + 63) = 0

⇒ (b − 36)(b + 63) = 0

⇒ b = 36 or b = −63 (Length/Breadth cannot be negative)

⇒ b = 36 m

**∴ The correct answer is 36 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of Rectangle

The total boundary length is given by P = 2 × (length + breadth).

Diagonal of Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is d = √(length² + breadth²).

Quadratic Roots shortcut

For x² + Sx + P = 0, the sum of roots is −S and the product is P.</p

questions.question: The diameter of a metallic solid sphere is 42 cm. It is melted and drawn into a wire with a cross-sectional diameter of 0.6 cm. Find the length (in metre) of the wire.

⇒ 12348 = 0.09 × L

⇒ L = 12348 ÷ 0.09 = 137200 cm

Slant Height of Cone

Volume of Cone

The volume of a cone is (1/3)πr²h, which is exactly one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height.</p

questions.question: A cube of side 10 cm is cut into cubes of side 2 cm. Calculate the total surface area (in cm²) of all the small cubes:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of small cubes (n³) = (Side of large cube / Side of small cube)³

Total Surface Area of all small cubes = n³ × 6 × (small side)²

⇒ (10 / 2)³ × 6 × 2² = 5³ × 6 × 4 = 125 × 24 = 3000 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3000 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Side of large cube (A) = 10 cm, Side of small cube (a) = 2 cm.

**Formula Used:** Volume of cube = side³; Total Surface Area (TSA) = 6 × side²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e73a59b38da958ea93ec83bb17abb90cbec09ad4b8964a3c41a0f5e426ae92b7.png] 

⇒ **Volume of large cube** = 10³ = 1000 cm³

⇒ **Volume of one small cube** = 2³ = 8 cm³

⇒ **Number of small cubes** = 1000 ÷ 8 = 125

⇒ **TSA of one small cube** = 6 × 2² = 6 × 4 = 24 cm²

⇒ **Total TSA of 125 cubes** = 125 × 24 = 3000 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3000 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cube Mensuration Formulas

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 4 × side² and the longest diagonal of a cube = √3 × side.

Volume Invariance

When a solid is recast or cut into smaller pieces, the **total volume** remains constant (VolumeLₐᵣgₑ = n × VolumeSₘₐₗₗ).

Surface Area Change

When a larger object is cut into smaller pieces, the **total surface area increases** because new faces are exposed.</p

questions.question:
If a hemisphere of radius 3 cm is fitted inside a cuboid and then water is filled inside the cuboid, the amount of water (in cm³) present in the cuboid is:

(Take π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **hemisphere** of radius **r** to be fitted inside a **cuboid**, the smallest cuboid must be a **cube** with side **a = 2r** (for base) and height **h = r**.

Volume of **water** = Volume of **cuboid** − Volume of **hemisphere**.

Volume = (2r × 2r × r) − (2/3 × π × r³) = 4r³ − (2/3 × 3.14 × r³).

Volume = r³ (4 − 2.0933) = 27 × 1.9067 ≈ 51.48 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.48 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Radius of hemisphere (r) = **3 cm**. π = **3.14**.

The **minimum dimensions** of the cuboid to fit the hemisphere are: Length = **6 cm**, Breadth = **6 cm**, and Height = **3 cm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3e3610c724070b5ca5651166253ba218e347991c317f8aea8afea783463cd61.png] 

⇒ Volume of **Cuboid** = Length × Breadth × Height = 6 × 6 × 3 = **108 cm³**.

⇒ Volume of **Hemisphere** = (2/3) × π × r³ = (2/3) × 3.14 × (3)³.

⇒ Volume of **Hemisphere** = 2 × 3.14 × 9 = **56.52 cm³**.

⇒ Volume of **Water** = 108 − 56.52 = **51.48 cm³**.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.48 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Sphere and Hemisphere

Volume of a sphere is (4/3)πr³ and for a hemisphere, it is exactly half: (2/3)πr³.

Fitting Solids in Containers

To fit a sphere of radius **r**, the minimum cube side is **2r**. For a hemisphere, the base requires **2r × 2r** but the height only needs **r**.

Surface Area of Hemisphere

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πr² and Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3πr².</p

questions.question: The area of a square is 2304 cm². Its perimeter is equal to the perimeter of a regular hexagon. what is the are (in cm²) of the hexagon?

Side of **square** = √2304 = 48 cm.

**Perimeter** of square = 4 × 48 = 192 cm.

Side of **hexagon** = 192 ÷ 6 = 32 cm.

Area of hexagon = 6 × (√3/4) × 32² = 1.5 × √3 × 1024 = 1536√3 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 1536√3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Area of square = 2304 cm². Perimeter of square = Perimeter of regular hexagon.

**Formula Used:** Area of square = a² | Perimeter of square = 4a | Perimeter of hexagon = 6s | Area of regular hexagon = (3√3/2)s²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac17dd1c2fa6955238fbb15ce628ffed716d474cc0940155b3025d8c06eece58.png] 

⇒ Side of square (a) = √2304 = 48 cm

⇒ Perimeter of square = 4 × 48 = 192 cm

⇒ Let side of hexagon be s. Then 6s = 192

⇒ s = 192 ÷ 6 = 32 cm

⇒ Area of hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 32²

⇒ Area = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 1024 = 3√3 × 512 = 1536√3 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1536√3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Regular Hexagon Properties

A regular hexagon consists of 6 **equilateral triangles**. Total area = 6 × (√3/4) × side².

Square Properties

Diagonal of a square = a√2. Area can also be expressed as (diagonal²)/2.

Perimeter Comparison

For a fixed perimeter, the **area increases** as the number of sides of a regular polygon increases (Circle has max area).</p

questions.question: The area of the base of a right circular cone is 3136 π cm² and its slant height is 65 cm. The curved surface area of the cone (in cm²) is:

**Calculations:**

⇒ πr² = 3136π

⇒ r² = 3136

Total Surface Area of Cone

It is the sum of the curved surface area and the base area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

Relation between h, r, and l

Perimeter of a Sector

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is half of its total surface area. If its height is 102 cm, then find its radius (in cm).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** is half of **Total Surface Area (TSA)**, then **CSA = TSA ÷ 2**.

This condition 2×**CSA** = **TSA** simplifies to 2×(2πrh) = 2πr(h + r).

Further simplification: 2h = h + r ⇒ **h = r**.

Since **height (h)** is 102 cm, the **radius (r)** must also be 102 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 102 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height (h)** of the cylinder = 102 cm

**Condition:** CSA = 1/2 × TSA

**Formula Used:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 2πrh

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 2πr(h + r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77dded3777171208b30142eda7cf20b958eda5eacaec742fe3cb9593cc5b001c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πrh = 1/2 × [2πr(h + r)]

⇒ 2πrh = πr(h + r)

⇒ 2h = h + r (By cancelling πr on both sides)

⇒ 2h − h = r

⇒ r = h

⇒ r = 102 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 102 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

The **volume** of a cylinder is the product of base area and height, given by V = πr²h.

Relationship between CSA and TSA

**Total Surface Area** is the sum of **Curved Surface Area** and the area of the two circular bases: TSA = CSA + 2×(πr²).

Hollow Cylinder

For a **hollow cylinder** with outer radius R and inner radius r, the Volume = π(R² − r²)h.</p
